Earlier reports suggested that Apple had abandoned the long-rumored all-glass iPhone, originally intended to mark the device's 20th anniversary. Bloomberg says the redesign is still on track for next year's Pro models. Here are the details.

Bloomberg says redesign is on track

Earlier today, investment research firm Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock, citing supply chain checks that the company had scrapped the rumored all-glass design for next year's iPhone 20th anniversary.

However, Bloomberg's latest report says the company "expects to release an iPhone Pro model next year with a new glass-like aesthetic," adding that "the front and back of the phone — internal codenames V73 and V74, respectively — will be made of glass, with the material extending around the sides and a metal bezel connecting them in the middle."

However, the report also notes that the project has been adjusted since it was first conceived:

The report directly refutes Jefferies' memo from earlier today, stating that "Apple's product roadmap has not changed."

What Jefferies said

Earlier today, Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said that, based on the firm's supply chain checks, the all-glass iPhone had been canceled due to poor production yields.

Lee described this development as a "significant setback" for Apple's efforts to drive higher-priced iPhones amid rising memory costs, and said canceling the plan could hurt Apple's ability to raise the average selling price and margins of its Pro models.

As a result, Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock and lowered its price target from $285.56 to $263.66; the previous price target had been cut from $308.92 on July 31, when Apple reported fiscal third-quarter 2026 results and issued cautious fourth-quarter guidance.
